However, he also expressed frustration about foreign influence over African economies and leadership structures. I don't like that the rest of the world owns so much of it and takes so much from it and no one speaks about it, he said. I'm really looking forward to hoping that the people running those different countries unite and take Africa back from the French, from the Spanish, from the Portuguese and the British. Hamilton has frequently visited Africa in recent years. During his 2024 mid-season break, he spent significant time in Senegal, describing the trip as heavy but deeply meaningful. Now, between 2001 and 2004, Sumatra lost 4.4 million hectares of forest. That's an area larger than Switzerland, making its landscapes increasingly vulnerable to landslides and flash flooding. Environmental groups warn that transferring land to state control does not guarantee better environmental practices. answer: Welcome back to Voltage Learning. Let's walk through this Intel analog engineer question because it touches on a very common bring-up issue that trips up even experienced designers. The question asks, during bring-up, an op-amp configured as a voltage follower shows an output that rails high even when the input is at mid-supply. Which condition most commonly causes this behavior? At first glance, this can feel confusing. After all, a voltage follower is supposed to simply mirror the input. But the key insight here is that negative feedback only works if the op-amp is operating within its valid input range. Even though the circuit uses feedback, the op-amp's input pins still must stay within the device's input common mode range. If the input voltage exceeds that range, often because the op-amp is not rail to rail on its inputs, the internal input stage can saturate. When that happens, the feedback loop effectively breaks down. The op-amp can no longer regulate properly, and the output often slams into one of the supply rails, frequently the positive rail during bring-up. Now, let's briefly rule out the other options. High open loop gain is normal and expected. It doesn't cause an output to rail by itself. Slew rate limits how fast the output can move, not where it settles in steady state. And a lighter output load actually makes it easier for the op-amp to drive the correct voltage, not harder. So the correct answer is, the input common mode exceeds the op-amp's valid range. This is exactly the kind of issue that shows up during early lab bring-up and silicon validation. Intel interviewers like this question because it tests whether you understand that data sheet limits still apply, even in seemingly simple configurations like voltage followers. answer: Fever is an elevation in body temperature mediated by hypothalamic pathways in the central nervous system. The hypothalamic thermoregulatory center controls body temperature through three mechanisms. One, controlling heat production mainly in the muscles and liver, two, controlling heat dissipation from the skin and lungs, and three, setting the normal body temperature. Fever is a physiologic process where the hypothalamus sets a higher body temperature set point in response to endogenous signaling. The body then rebalances heat production and dissipation to elevate the body temperature to the new set point. This is why patients with new fevers often feel cold and experience rigors. Their current body temperature, although elevated above true normal, lies below the newly elevated hypothalamic set point and leads to the subjective feeling of cold.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Seeing a red light on your AirPods Pro 3 charging case, it's a signal from the case's LED indicator about the charging or battery status. A solid red light usually means the case battery is critically low, below 10%, and needs charging. If you see a flashing red light, this often indicates a charging error, potentially due to a faulty lightning port, incompatible charger, or an internal issue. While charging, the light should turn amber/orange, indicating normal charging, and then green when fully charged. Basically, the red light is a diagnostic indicator to alert you of a problem with power or charging. If you encounter a red light, first try resetting your AirPods via the Bluetooth settings on your paired device. Next, clean the charging port with a soft dry brush to remove any debris that might be interfering with the connection. Then, use a different charging cable and adapter. Ideally, use Apple's USB-C to lightning adapter as the Pro 3 supports both lightning and USB-C magsafe. Also, ensure your AirPods Pro 3 firmware is up to date via your paired iOS device. If the red light persists, it might indicate a hardware fault. In that case, contact Apple support or an authorized service provider, especially if the device is still under warranty, which has been extended to two years in some cases due to reported manufacturing defects.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: From the 12th of October 2025, the EU will introduce new border checks known as the entry exit system, EES. As a part of its plans to strengthen border security, this is a new digital border system that will change requirements for British and other non-EU citizens traveling to the Schengen area, which encompasses all EU countries except for Cyprus and Ireland. It will also include the non-EU states, Iceland, Norway, Switzerland, and Liechtenstein. The entry exit system is an automated IT system designed to register non-EU nationals traveling for short stays of up to 90 days in every 180 days. It will be used every time an individual crosses the external borders of any of the following countries. When EES is introduced, you may need to create a digital record on your first visit to the Schengen area at the port or airport on arrival. This will involve submitting your fingerprints, having your photo taken, and your passport scanned at dedicated booths. This new system will be introduced in phases over the first six months, and will eventually replace the current system of manually stamping passports when visitors arrive in the EU. You will not need to provide any information before traveling. At the port of Dover, Eurotunnel and Folkestone and Eurostar from St. Pancras, EES will be carried out before departure, as is currently the case for border checks. EES may take a few extra minutes to complete, so be prepared to wait during busy times at the border once the system starts. You can check with your travel operator to find out whether EES will affect your journey. Once registered, your digital record will be valid for three years. If you enter the Schengen area again during this time, you will only need to provide one biometric, either a photo or a fingerprint, at the border when you enter or exit. For more information, visit gov.uk/entry-exit system.

Strangers become friends, and the desert becomes a place of freedom, creativity, and unity. The playa is a living art gallery. Giant wooden temples tower over the desert floor. Mechanical dragons breathe fire, and surreal neon structures glow against the night sky. Art cars, transformed into moving sculptures, carry dancers and lights through the dust. Everything here is created by participants, and nothing is left behind. From sunrise yoga and meditation to all-night raves, Burning Man pulses with sound and movement. DJs spin under laser beams, drummers pound in circles, and fire spinners light up the night. The energy is raw and electric, a celebration of music, creativity, and life itself in the middle of the desert. At the festival's peak, the Man, a towering wooden effigy, is set ablaze in front of tens of thousands. Flames rise, sparks scatter across the desert sky, and cheers echo through the playa. Another sacred fire consumes the temple, a space for reflection and remembrance. And then, just as quickly, Black Rock City disappears, leaving only dust, memories, and the spirit of Burning Man.

answer: Once upon a time, in the wild landscapes of Tasmania, lived the thylacine, also called the Tasmanian tiger for the dark stripes across its back. Despite its wolf-like face, the thylacine was actually a marsupial, carrying its young in a pouch, just like kangaroos. It was the largest carnivorous marsupial of modern times, a shy and nocturnal hunter that fed on small animals and birds. Unlike dogs or wolves, its jaw could open to an astonishing 80 degrees, giving it a fearsome bite. Sadly, European settlers saw the thylacine as a threat to sheep and livestock. By the late 1800s, there were even government bounties that encouraged hunting. Disease, habitat loss, and competition with dogs only made things worse. The last known thylacine lived in Beaumaris Zoo in Hobart. Filmed in 1933 by naturalist David Fleay, it died just three years later, in 1936. That moment marked the end of a species that had survived for thousands of years. Today, the thylacine remains a powerful symbol of extinction and a reminder of the importance of protecting endangered wildlife before it's too late.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: How do product reviews compare to official appliance ratings? Have you ever wondered how product reviews stack up against official appliance ratings? Let's break it down so you can make informed choices when shopping for home appliances. Official appliance ratings come from independent organizations or testing labs. These ratings are created using standardized methods to evaluate appliances. They focus on measurable factors like performance, energy efficiency, durability, and reliability. The testing is consistent across all products in a category, which allows for straightforward comparisons. You can expect detailed data from these ratings, and they are conducted without any influence from manufacturers. This means you receive unbiased and objective information. On the other hand, product reviews, especially those from users or customers, reflected individual experiences with appliances in real-world settings. These reviews can give you a glimpse into everyday use, customer satisfaction, and practical issues like ease of use and noise levels. However, the quality of user reviews can vary widely. Some may be subjective or influenced by personal expectations. You might find reviews that are overly positive or negative, which may not representing the typical experience. Professional review sites and consumer organizations often combine both methods. They conduct their own tests while also considering user feedback. By purchasing appliances as regular customers, they avoid any bias from manufacturers. This results in ratings that are both data-driven and reflective of actual usage. When it comes to home appliances, relying on official ratings helps you understand the technical performance and reliability of a product. Meanwhile, product reviews can highlight real-life advantages or issues that might not show up in lab tests. For instance, you might learn about customer service quality or how well an appliance fits into a typical household environment. So, how can you use this information when choosing home appliances? Start by looking at official ratings to narrow down your options based on objective performance and efficiency. After that, check out product reviews to learn about user experiences, common problems, and satisfaction levels. By combining both sources, you can make a more informed purchase decision that balances technical quality with everyday usability.

answer: A World War II themed movie has taken audiences by storm, moving viewers to tears while earning widespread praise from critics and fans alike. Released in 2019, Jojo Rabbit has been hailed as a cinematic masterpiece, one that blends humor and heartbreak in a truly unique way. Directed by Taika Waititi, the film is a satirical coming-of-age story set during the final years of Nazi Germany. At its heart is Jojo, a 10-year-old boy who, indoctrinated by Nazi propaganda, idolizes Adolf Hitler, imagining him as his comical, imaginary best friend. But everything changes when Jojo discovers a Jewish girl hiding in his attic. This discovery forces him to question everything he believes, setting the stage for an emotional and often absurd journey of self-discovery. Viewers have described the film as a powerful blend of laughter and sorrow. One IMDB reviewer wrote, it was hilarious and heartfelt. The acting was superb, the story was thought-provoking. It was funny at times and heartbreaking at others. Another called the film moving, hilarious, tragic, admitting they had doubts at first but trusted Waititi's vision. The emotional roller coaster is real, they added, praising the film's originality and depth. I laughed and I cried, another fan confessed. This film was exceptional, one of the best I've seen this year. Waititi's comedic vision is brilliant, and the cast is phenomenal. The cast includes Roman Griffin Davis in his breakout role as Jojo, Thomasin McKenzie, Sam Rockwell, Rebel Wilson, Stephen Merchant, Alfie Allen, and Scarlett Johansson, with Waititi himself portraying a ridiculous, imaginary version of Hitler. Adapted from Christine Leunens' novel Caging Skies, Waititi initially drafted the script in 2011. Though the original version was much darker, it evolved into a black comedy that could balance satire with genuine emotion. Filming took place in 2018, and the movie premiered the following year to critical acclaim. Jojo Rabbit earned multiple awards, including the Academy Award for best adapted screenplay, making Waititi the first Marry filmmaker to win in that category. Audiences and critics have since labeled it a must watch film, especially for fans of war dramas told from a fresh and human perspective. From laughter to despair, Jojo Rabbit manages to confront the horrors of war through the innocent lens of a child, making it a standout film that resonates long after the credits roll.

answer: What is the Adidas Firebird tracksuit? Have you ever wondered how a simple tracksuit became a cultural icon in hip-hop fashion? The Adidas Firebird tracksuit is a perfect example of this phenomenon. Originally launched in the 1980s, this tracksuit features the iconic three stripes along the sleeves and pant legs. It evolved from earlier Adidas styles, such as the Beckenbauer tracksuit, and quickly became a symbol of athletic excellence and street style. The Firebird tracksuit typically consists of a zip-up jacket and matching pants made from shiny polyester fabric. This sleek and sporty look made it a favorite among athletes and fashion enthusiasts alike. In hip-hop culture, the Firebird tracksuit holds a special place as a cultural emblem. During the 1980s, it became closely associated with the emerging hip-hop scene, especially among B-boys, MCS, and break dancers. The tracksuit was embraced for its comfort and durability, which suited the dynamic movements of breakdancing and the expressive fashion of hip-hop artists. One of the most significant moments linking the Adidas Firebird tracksuit to hip-hop came from the legendary rap group Run-DMC from Queens, New York. They famously wore the Firebird tracksuit as part of their signature look, pairing it with Adidas Superstar sneakers and gold chains. This image became iconic and helped establish the tracksuit as the unofficial uniform of old-school hip-hop. Run-DMC's 1986 hit, My Adidas, celebrated the brand and its connection to their identity. This song led to the first major endorsement deal between a music group and a sportswear company, marking a turning point in both music and fashion. The Firebird tracksuit's influence extended beyond just fashion. It symbolized authenticity, street credibility, and unity within the hip-hop community. It bridged the gap between sportswear and music culture, making Adidas a staple brand in hip-hop fashion. Even today, the Firebird tracksuit is revered as a retro classic that represents the roots of hip-hop style. It continues to be worn and celebrated by artists and fans alike. The Adidas Firebird tracksuit is more than just athletic wear. It is a cultural icon that helped define hip-hop fashion in the 1980s and remains a symbol of the genre's early style and attitude.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: From album of the year to the biggest stage in sports, Bad Bunny just turned the Super Bowl halftime show into a full-on celebration of Puerto Rico. But one detail from his outfit has fans talking, the number 64 stitched onto his jersey. So what does it mean? The show featured surprise appearances from Lady Gaga and Ricky Martin and transformed the field into a vibrant tribute to Puerto Rican culture. Style-wise, the details were just as intentional. He wore an Audemars Piguet watch, a Marquis diamond stud earring by Marvin Douglas, designed to echo the shape of a football, and a custom white football jersey by Zara. The jersey featured the name Ocasio, a nod to his real name Benito Antonio Martinez Ocasio. And now there's more clarity around the number 64 stitched across his chest. According to Complex, Bad Bunny was paying tribute to his late uncle, who previously played football and wore the same number. Before that detail emerged, fans had floated several theories. Some believed the number referenced his mother's birth year. Others connected it to the initial, widely criticized death toll reported after Hurricane Maria devastated Puerto Rico in 2017. There were even historical interpretations, including a nod to the 64th United States Congress, which passed the Jones-Shafroth Act granting U.S. citizenship to Puerto Ricans in 1917. Some pointed to 2023 when Bad Bunny's Un Verano Sin Ti became the first Spanish language album ever nominated for Album of the Year at the 64th Grammy Awards. At the 2026 Grammys, he made history again, winning Album of the Year for De Mi Tirar Mas Fotos, the first Spanish-language album to ever take home the top prize. That same night, he also turned heads on the red carpet in Schiaparelli's first-ever menswear design, and used his acceptance speech to protest ICE, declaring, we are humans and we are Americans. Those moments echoed into the halftime show, where he appeared to symbolically present his Grammy to a child watching his speech on a small TV, a powerful visual about legacy and representation. NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell later praised the artist, saying Bad Bunny understood the weight of the platform and its power to unite people. Ahead of the game, an emotional Bad Bunny said the performance was about joy, culture, and heart, and dedicated it to those who came before him. With this latest confirmation, the meaning appears deeply personal, a family tribute layered into a performance already packed with cultural pride, history, and legacy.

answer: The lake gave no sign. For centuries, the waters of Iznik rippled softly against the edge of a city once called Nicaea, birthplace of Christian creed, stage for imperial councils, and grave to forgotten martyrs. Nothing in the breeze, the current, or the reflection hinted at what lay beneath. But in 2014, a drone camera flew low over the water and found a church sleeping just below the surface. 50 meters from the shore, in water barely 3 meters deep, rose the submerged skeleton of a Basilica. Its stone walls followed a familiar pattern, three aisles, east-facing aps, a square narthex, a structure from the early 5th century CE, built shortly after the first Council of Nicea had rewritten the rules of heaven. Scholars now believe it was dedicated to St. Neophytos, a young martyr said to have been killed on that very shoreline, stabbed and abandoned in the shallows for refusing to renounce his faith. The Basilica's shape suggests reverence, but its fate speaks otherwise. In the year 740, an earthquake shattered the region, temples fell, walls cracked, and this church, already fragile on marshy ground, collapsed into the lake and vanished from memory. No chronicler recorded its loss, no pilgrimage map marked its name. For 1,300 years, it lay beneath the water like a cathedral entombed in silence. But even underwater, the clues remained. In 2025, excavators confirmed its identity as the church of the Holy Fathers, possibly built near or over the site of the council itself. Around it, archaeologists found burials, eight tombs lined with terracotta tiles tucked beneath the nave and apse. Infants, children, adults, laid in sacred shadow as if hoping to sleep close to a martyr's bones. And just beyond the ruin a pendant surfaced, its face worn but still clear. St. Nicholas carried by a pilgrim and dropped in reverence or fear. Yet the past here is layered. Beneath the Basilica, some believe are the foundations of a forgotten Apollo temple. Others whisper of a Senate palace where emperor once spoke of salvation. And still others suspect the site predates all of them, a shrine built atop a necropolis, where holiness was measured by how long the dead had waited. No inscriptions remain, no relics speak. Only stones pressed flat by silt and time, held in place by the lake's stillness. But when drought comes, as it has in recent years, the water recedes, the basilica rises again. Columns break the surface, the apse returns to light. For a brief moment, the church is no longer drowned, just exposed. Plans exist now for an underwater museum. Glass walkways suspended above the nave, viewing chambers, lit vaults where visitors may pray or simply witness. But for now, it remains where it was found, submerged, weightless, intact. A sanctuary that did not fall from grace, but was carried into it.

While primitive by modern standards, the VDNKH robots played a significant role in robotics history, demonstrating early concepts of autonomous behavior and human-robot interaction that would influence future development.

answer: When we were creating imagery for the Nvidia CES keynote, one of our goals was to create a high-fidelity group shot of 20 specific robots. We realized early on that a primary technical challenge was pixel density. Current generative models are limited to 4K or 5K resolution. So each robot occupied too small an area for fine detail. For this major keynote, we also needed a flexible workflow that allowed for rapid iterations without rebuilding the entire scene. Here's how we solved it. We began by generating low fidelity 3D models from reference images. While these were rough placeholders, they provided exactly what we needed to establish the initial layout for every robot in the set. Then, we brought these models into 3D software to assemble the scene. This gave us the flexibility to explore different compositions with total accuracy and control before committing to high resolution assets. Once the layout was locked, we exported the scene. While the final lighting and fine robot details weren't perfect, the scene gave us the precise coordinates we needed. We took the exact angle of every robot and went back to our reference images to generate fully detailed 4K individual assets that fit the composition perfectly. In Photoshop, we reconstructed the layout using these high-quality robot images. The result was a clean, high fidelity composition where every element was sharp and correctly positioned. Next, we used Weavy to build a custom AI agent that let us rapidly iterate on various lighting themes. Once the creative direction was settled, we generated the full 4K scene with the final look and lighting, then upscaled it to 12K. Given the complexity of generating 20 characters in a single pass, we took a targeted approach to the robot details, regenerating our high-detail robot assets specifically to match the new lighting environment and integrate seamlessly into the final composition. We brought these light-matched high detail robots back into Photoshop and merged them into the composition to restore all the lost texture and sharpness. After final touch ups to clean the scene, we produced a massive 12K high detail environment built specifically for the giant keynote screen. This workflow allowed us to handle change requests rapidly, maintain full control over the composition, look, and detail of every individual component, and bring the scene to life just as we had envisioned.

This section provides a fantastic platform for local filmmakers to present their work to both local and international audiences. Attendees often have the chance to meet filmmakers and actors, which adds to the festival's charm. The audience also gets to vote for the best films in various categories, while an official jury awards the festival's main prizes, including the coveted Redentor trophy. The festival is held across multiple cinemas in Rio de Janeiro, making it accessible to a broad audience. In addition to film screenings, Festival do Rio often includes debates, special sessions, and lectures. These events contribute to the cultural and audiovisual development of the city. The festival plays a vital role in strengthening Rio's position in the audiovisual sector and promoting Brazilian culture on both national and international stages. Overall, the Rio de Janeiro International Film Festival is a major cultural event that celebrates cinema, supports local filmmakers, and connects audiences with both global and regional film production. Goods were traded around the world, and in return, exotic goods from the far corners of the globe were imported. If you were part of the middle class, it was a time of plenty and a cornucopia of goods from all over the world could be purchased at one of the latest innovations, the department store. Ivory goods from the Orient, ebony from darkest Africa, sandwich glass from Massachusetts, coffee from Brazil, porcelain from the Orient. Of all the products available to the well-to-do in the Victorian age, one of the most indispensable was whale oil. Its superior lubricating qualities made whale oil the ideal product to keep industrial steam engines operating. But whale oil was also used on the domestic front. Whale oil lamps lit up the homes of the wealthy and fashionable. It provided a brighter light than other animal fats available and produced far less smoke. Whale oil was extensively used in toiletries, cosmetics, and soaps. While whale oil was highly prized, whale bone too was a much sought-after product. In many ways, whale bone was the plastic of its day. It was strong and flexible and could be put to numerous uses. Whalebone was used to make buggy whips, as well as the springs on which the carriages rode. It was used to make brushes, combs, the ribs for parasols and umbrellas, and fishing rods. answer: Flat-headed cats have been successfully detected and filmed in southern Thailand for the first time in almost 30 years. Most exciting of all, the observations included a female flat-headed cat with her cub. Flat-headed cats are the smallest in Southeast Asia. They weigh half that of a typical domestic cat and have a distinctive flattened forehead and elongated skull. They are small, nocturnal and prefer to occupy dense terrain, making searching for them in the wild that much harder. Even catching them on camera traps can be difficult. But using lessons learned from studying fishing cats, Panthera were able to identify the best sites for camera placement, leading to the successful detection and photographic evidence of the flat-headed cat. It's estimated there are 2,500 flat-headed cats globally, and they're classed as endangered by the IUCN, but in Thailand, it was considered possibly extinct. During that storm, floodwaters inundated the Blue Bannan Line and even swamped Taipei Main Station, reaching depths of up to 2.3 m. The disaster led Taipei Rapid Transit Corporation to design and install multiple waterproof systems across the network. If flooding threatens, this watertight door, 30 cm thick, can be closed to prevent water from entering the platform level, said CTS reporter Chang Hsiaoyun, while demonstrating the mechanism on site. According to Huang Yi Chao, a section chief from the Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit systems, the doors were introduced after engineers realized that flooding could easily overwhelm stations entrances. We decided to place basic waterproofing at the entrances and add full seal floodgates at station interfaces, he explained. The Taipei Rapid Transit Corporation uses several types of flood barriers, including swinging, vertical, and sliding models, to block water from penetrating underground areas. Although forecasts predict less rain from this week's Typhoon Fung Wong than from Nari, with expected totals around 300 mm over 2 days, city officials said the metro system remains on high alert to ensure uninterrupted service. Filip Stawski for ICRT News.

The East German government initially denied plans to build a wall, with leaders like Walter Ulbricht claiming there was no intention to do so. As the wall went up, journalists reported on this contradiction, illustrating the propaganda battles happening alongside the physical construction. International coverage also focused on the broader Cold War tensions. Reports described US troop movements and the famous tank confrontation at Checkpoint Charlie later that year. Journalists framed the wall as a symbol of communist oppression and the deep ideological divide between East and West. During the 1960s, coverage was full of urgency and emotion. Reporters told stories of fear, hope, and resilience of Berliners living through one of the Cold War's most defining moments. They combined eyewitness accounts with political analysis, capturing the era's style of reporting. This area is famous for its dramatic granite peaks and lush pine forests, creating a striking backdrop for many scenes. The unique scenery adds depth to the film, making it visually captivating.
Another key filming site is the Anji Bamboo Forest in Zhejiang province. This serene forest is known for its lush bamboo groves, providing a tranquil environment that perfectly complements the film's more peaceful moments. The beauty of this location truly enhances the film's aesthetic.
Beijing, the capital city of China, also played a role in the filming process. The urban landscape of Beijing contributed to the cultural aspects of the story, showcasing the blend of tradition and modernity in Chinese life.
Chengde, located in Hebei province, was another filming location. This city offers a mix of historical and natural settings, which helped to create the film's rich visual narrative. The combination of these diverse locations allowed the filmmakers to capture the essence of Chinese culture.
Additionally, Hengdian World Studios in Zhejiang province was utilized for creating elaborate sets. As the largest film studio in the world, it provided the facilities needed to recreate traditional Chinese architecture and settings. This studio played a vital role in bringing the film's story to life.
Together, these locations contributed to the film's success, highlighting China's rich cultural heritage and stunning natural beauty. Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon is not just a film. It is a celebration of Chinese arts and performing arts, making it a significant part of Chinese cinema history. What birds can you see in the Masai Mara?
Have you ever wondered what birds you might encounter in the stunning Masai Mara? This incredible region in Kenya is a paradise for bird lovers, boasting over 580 recorded species. The variety of habitats here, from open savanna to wetlands, supports an amazing range of birds. Let's start with the impressive birds of prey. The Masai Mara is home to many eagle species. You might spot the Tawny Eagle, Steppe Eagle, and Imperial Eagle soaring above. Other raptors include the African Hawk-Eagle and Verreaux's Eagle. If you keep your eyes peeled, you may also see the Bat Hawk and several types of buzzards like the Common Buzzard and Long-legged Buzzard. As you wander through the grasslands, look out for the large ground birds. The Common Ostrich is a prominent sight, strutting across the savanna. Near the rivers and wetlands, you can find various waterfowl. Keep an eye out for the White-faced Whistling Duck and the Northern Pintail among others. Wading birds are also abundant in the Masai Mara. Plover and lapwing species are often seen near water bodies. You might encounter the Little Ringed Plover and the Kittlitz's Plover. The Blacksmith Lapwing and the Spur-winged Lapwing are also common in these areas. In the wetlands, look for the Greater Painted-snipe and the African Jacana. These birds thrive in the lush environments created by the rivers and marshes. The diversity of birds here reflects the rich ecological variety of the Masai Mara. The different habitats, including riverine forests and acacia woodlands, provide food and nesting sites for many species. This makes the Masai Mara a vital area for bird survival and reproduction. The presence of various raptors indicates a healthy ecosystem with plenty of prey. For birdwatchers, the Masai Mara offers a unique opportunity to see a wide range of African birdlife in one location. Whether you are a seasoned birder or just starting, this region is a must-visit for anyone interested in birds. With its rich diversity and stunning scenery, the Masai Mara truly is a birding hotspot in Kenya.

answer: Back in the early 2000s, Capcom dropped Metal Walker onto the Game Boy Color and I gotta admit, I thought I had stumbled on some hidden mecha brawler gem. With a name like Metal Walker, you expect something gritty and full of robotic smackdowns, right? Well, you do get robots, but it's more like a Pokemon and a game of pool had a weird random baby. So here's the setup. You play as a kid looking for your dad on an island filled with relics from a mysterious metal called core. As you travel the island, you'll have a companion Metal Walker who's your little battle bot buddy that levels up and evolves based on core units. There are three types, land, marine, and sky. You can switch out orbs to give your bot new abilities. Some will let you smash rocks, one will let you cross water, and each one has different stats to tweak your strategy. Cool in theory, right? Now, the combat is where this game gets totally bonkers. It plays out on a top-down battlefield where instead of picking attacks from a menu, you'll launch your metal walker into enemies billiard style. You'll bounce off walls, collide with opponents, trigger environmental hazards, and hope RNG Jesus is on your side. Each round, a handful of random items spawn on the field, some helpful, some annoying, and by the way, enemies can pick them up too. So it can get chaotic pretty fast. Lining up a good shot is harder than you think, especially with the physics not quite behaving the way you would want it to. Add in the relentless encounter rate and you end up in constant fights that feel more like a chore than a challenge. I found myself wishing I could just turn it down a notch just so I can explore for more than 10 seconds. Speaking of exploration, this isn't a game where you can get lost. The NPCs give clear instructions on how to progress and the descriptions of places are pretty spot on. There's a neat mechanic where you can analyze enemies mid-battle to get new parts, which is probably the closest thing this game has to catching Pokémon. I ended up using a GameFAQs guide because some of the fights were getting too punishing without a bit of extra help. And trust me, the guide made a big difference. There are cheats available if you have a Game Genie or Game Shark. I didn't use any because I really do enjoy leveling up. Visually, Metal Walker is clean for a Game Boy Color title. The sprites are pretty sharp, and it all fits the sci-fi theme. The music was surprisingly great with a large soundtrack you won't get bored with. After all this praise, is it worth it? Honestly, no. The battle system is unique enough to keep me intrigued, but it's not the mecha brawler I expected. So, unless you're a collector or just dying for a fresh take on RPGs, you're better off watching a video or just reading about it.

NATO leaders endorsed a new target of allocating 5% of GDP to defense spending by 2035, a sharp rise from the previous 2% goal. This decision addresses both Trump's demands and concerns over increasing threats from Russia following its 2022 invasion of Ukraine. The official statement reaffirmed NATO's ironclad commitment to Article 5, declaring that an attack on one member is an attack on all. Trump had previously caused alarm by saying there were numerous definitions of the clause, but at the summit, he reassured allies, stating, we're with them all the way. NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte acknowledged the financial challenge for European nations and Canada but emphasized its necessity, citing the current international security climate. Rutte, the former Dutch Prime Minister, noted full backing from NATO members, though Spain insisted it could meet its obligations without hitting the 5% mark, a stance Rutte diplomatically accepted to keep the summit smooth. President Trump praised the deal, calling it a great victory for everybody, and highlighting that nations were finally aligning with his long-standing call for increased contributions. The summit was choreographed to maintain harmony, including shortening official proceedings and hosting Trump at the Royal Palace. Trump described the hosts, King Willem Alexander and Queen Maxima, as beautiful and spectacular and posted positively about the event on Truth Social. Belgium's Prime Minister Bart De Wever labeled the spending hike as historic, urging Europe to take greater responsibility for its security. Trump also met briefly with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, referring to him as a nice guy and claimed ongoing discussions with Russian President Vladimir Putin. answer: On the 17th of October 1814, a strange and destructive event took place at the Moe and Co. S Horseshoe brewery, located at the junction of Tottenham Court Road and Oxford Street in London, England. The brewery contained several enormous wooden vats, some of them 22 feet tall, filled with porter, a dark London beer that was extremely popular during that period. On that day, the hoop of one of the huge vats suddenly broke, causing the vat to burst and release its contents. The force of the escaping beer ruptured the stopcock of a second large vat, which also began to discharge. Several other vats were damaged in the chain reaction. In total, between 580,000 and 1,470,000 liters of porter flooded out, smashing through the brewery's rear wall, which was 25 ft high. Behind the brewery stood the St. Giles's rookery, one of London's poorest and most crowded slum districts. Once the wall collapsed, a wave of porter about 15 ft high swept into New Street and Great Russell Street, destroying homes and flooding basements. Everyone inside the brewery survived, but according to the coroner's report, eight people in the surrounding neighborhood were killed either by drowning, injuries from collapsing walls, or being trapped in flooded rooms. Eyewitnesses described the area afterwards as looking like the aftermath of an earthquake. Rumors later spread of people collecting the spilled beer, widespread drunkenness, and even deaths from alcohol poisoning in the following days. However, these stories appear exaggerated. The corner ruled that the disaster was an act of God, meaning the brewery was not held legally responsible and paid no compensation. The incident contributed to the decline of large wooden fermentation vats, which were eventually phased out across the brewing industry. The horseshoe brewery was later demolished. Today, the Dominion theater stands on the former site of the brewery. Thank you for watching.
